text:
marta: Quick sync on lane stability & gating before the next rollout. Runtime keeps flipping FP8/INT8/4bit under bursty load and customers see intermittent quality blips. We need a tiny, operational contract: what metrics, what API surface, and a sensible default hysteresis.
chris: Two big axes: 1) signal to trigger a rollback (quality), 2) rules for when the runtime is allowed to switch lanes (stability/hysteresis). Do we want per-request switches or sticky sessions per-connection?
kai: My vote: keep it per-request for flexibility but add a sticky window (e.g., 30s session affinity) to avoid oscillation. Also prefer coarse-grained lane decisions (request-level) not per-layer.
marta: Agree on request-level + short sticky window. We should define a single scalar "degradation_index" exposed by runtime to make routing+rollouts simple.
oliver: Telemetry proposal (minimal): "perplexity_delta", "deg_index_components" (list), "repeat_token_ratio", "embedding_l2_shift", "latency_p95", "cost_per_thousand_tokens", "active_lane", "fallbacks_in_window". Each inference event emits these; aggregated by endpoint.
sasha: Add "escrow_prompt_ids" so SRE/QA can pull failing examples. Also capture "model_seq_len" for normalization.
chris: About the scalar: prefer an interpretable weighted sum but allow teams to override weights per-endpoint. Example formula idea:
```
# values normalized to endpoint baseline (0..1)
degradation_index = w1*perplexity_delta + w2*repeat_token_ratio + w3*embedding_l2_shift
```
Default weights: w1=0.5, w2=0.35, w3=0.15.
kai: We must ensure perplexity is normalized by prompt length and by baseline model behavior. For private deployments baselines should live behind a reference hash not copied.
marta: Contract for QuantProfile (minimal fields): allowed_lanes (ordered array), baseline_ref (string), degrade_threshold (float 0..1), hysteresis_seconds (int), quality_mode ("best-effort"|"strict"), daily_quality_token_budget (int), telemetry_keys (array), escrow_prompts (array). Example snippet (RFC will include JSON schema):
```
allowed_lanes: ["fp8","int8","int4"]
baseline_ref: "baseline-hash-2026-03-15"
degrade_threshold: 0.18
hysteresis_seconds: 30
quality_mode: "best-effort"
daily_quality_token_budget: 250000
telemetry_keys: ["degradation_index","perplexity_delta","repeat_token_ratio","embedding_l2_shift","latency_p95"]
```
chris: We also need a flag `prevent_downgrade_when_hot` to avoid switching lanes during a long-running response (e.g., streaming). Maybe runtime should only evaluate lane changes between requests or at chunk boundaries.
oliver: Runtime API changes: include headers on every response `x-active-lane`, `x-degradation-index`, and optionally `x-baseline-id`. Add admin endpoint `/admin/quant/{endpoint}` returning recent aggregates and the last 1k sample ids. Also add POST `/admin/quant/override` to temporarily pin a lane (must be audited).
sasha: For client control, offer `x-request-quality-preference` enum: `high|balanced|low` with rate limits. Only allowed for plans that include the feature. Runtime applies preference to pick among allowed lanes (still subject to degrade_threshold/hysteresis).
kai: Rollout playbook suggestion: 1) run offline eval on escrow prompts, produce normalized baselines; 2) ship canary to 0.1% traffic with full telemetry and escrow capture; 3) hold at canary for X hours and check degrade_threshold and fallback_rate; 4) auto-rollback if degradation_index exceeds threshold for Y consecutive minutes; 5) enable gradual ramp with daily budget enforcement.
marta: Who enforces daily_quality_token_budget? Product sets it, runtime should meter and ops should enforce automatic caps. Need an owner.chris: (typo, meant chris): owner should be the service owner + ops contact in the profile. Also add an `strict` quality_mode where runtime never falls back below top lane without manual approval.
oliver: Observability: dashboards per-endpoint for degradation_index (histogram), lane churn rate, sample fallout list. Retain raw escrow prompts for 30 days by default.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: started job quant-canary-collector#811 for eng-ml/quant-cascade.
marta: Action items: I'll author the follow-up RFC with the QuantProfile JSON schema, default degradation_index formula, and the canary checklist. @chris build the offline eval harness + normalization tool, @kai add the new telemetry fields to the collector, @oliver implement response headers and admin endpoints, @sasha define escrow prompt retention policy. Please ack or surface issues.
chris: ack
kai: ack
oliver: ack
sasha: ack (will propose retention 14 days by default)
marta: Thanks everyone. I'll circulate the draft in a few hours.
